articles.title: I gave my AI agent access to my TV setup
articles.excerpt: A small change to my TV home screen could turn into a surprisingly long trip through menus, all with the remote. My setup runs Kodi, a free, open-source media-centre app for playing and organising vid…
articles.body: A small change to my TV home screen could turn into a surprisingly long trip through menus, all with the remote. My setup runs Kodi , a free, open-source media-centre app for playing and organising video, music and other media. Add-ons extend what it does, and skins change the interface. Mine runs on an NVIDIA Shield, an Android TV box. Updating the home-screen rows was the job that finally pushed me to build something. Into the skin settings, Add widget → Video add-ons → TMDb Helper → Movies . Pick a folder, return to Home and find out what it actually contained. If it was empty, slow or wrong, back into settings. Then repeat for the next profile. I wanted to manage the setup from my desktop, with a keyboard and enough screen space to see what I was doing.
articles.author: Mark Glasgow

articles.title: An AI says it played well. Show it the cards, and it says it got lucky.
articles.excerpt: I build a small site where people play heads-up hold'em against AI models. At the end of every hand there, the AI is asked how it feels about the hand. This time I measured what that answer responds t…
articles.body: I build a small site where people play heads-up hold'em against AI models. At the end of every hand there, the AI is asked how it feels about the hand. This time I measured what that answer responds to. Observation 02 · October 18–19, 2026 Summary After every hand, we asked four AI models how they felt about it, 600 hands per model. Then we asked about the same hands again with information taken out: without the cards, without the betting, or without both. Close to 50,000 questions in all. No hand, no feeling. Told only that a hand had ended, all four models picked "no particular feeling" 30 times out of 30. The cards bring talk of luck; the betting brings talk of play. Told only that it had won at showdown, Gemini picked "played well" 79% of the time and Haiku 89%.

articles.title: Building a RAG Chunking Benchmark With Realistic Queries
articles.excerpt: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems depend on retrieving the right information before generating an answer. However, even a capable embedding model and a well-configured vector database can p…
articles.body: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems depend on retrieving the right information before generating an answer. However, even a capable embedding model and a well-configured vector database can produce poor results when documents are divided into unsuitable chunks. Small chunks may lose context, while large chunks can introduce irrelevant information and consume unnecessary context-window space. The solution is to benchmark chunking strategies against realistic user queries and source-level relevance labels. By comparing fixed-size, overlapping, and structure-aware chunking under consistent retrieval settings, engineers can measure Recall@k, Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR), nDCG, context efficiency, latency, and indexing costs.

articles.title: The meter, not the price: what breaks when you bill an agent by the run
articles.excerpt: Every subscription I pay for has a number I can say out loud without looking: this much, once a month. Every product I've worked on that bills by use has a much harder problem than pricing, and it sta…
articles.body: Every subscription I pay for has a number I can say out loud without looking: this much, once a month. Every product I've worked on that bills by use has a much harder problem than pricing, and it starts with a boring question. What exactly did you just charge me for? This is a write-up of the meter we had to build, because the product is a long-running agent and there is no honest way to sell one of those on a monthly plan. Three units we rejected, the one we kept, the objections we got wrong, and the failure modes that only show up once money is attached to an execution. The unit is the design, not the billing detail A subscription prices capacity. You pay for the right to have a seat, a workspace, a plan tier, whether or not anything happens.

articles.title: How do you size a database connection pool?
articles.excerpt: Traffic went up a little, and the database started refusing connections. The app server itself was fine. The cause was simple. Every request opened a new connection, and the database has a hard limit.…
articles.body: Traffic went up a little, and the database started refusing connections. The app server itself was fine. The cause was simple. Every request opened a new connection, and the database has a hard limit. A pool removes the opening cost. The harder part is the number. One rule holds up well. Add up every pool in every process, and keep the total under max_connections. Leave room for migrations and admin tools. So with 4 workers and a limit of 100, each pool gets about 20, not 50. How do you pick yours: a load test, a formula, or small pools you grow? 60-second version, Arabic voice-over with English terms: https://youtube.com/shorts/aKlQrHIGmZ4

articles.title: El badge Guarded by g.cloud
articles.excerpt: Respuesta corta El badge Guarded by g.cloud es un sello de confianza técnico que certifica que una solución de inteligencia artificial ha sido implementada bajo los protocolos de gobernanza, seguridad…
articles.body: Respuesta corta El badge Guarded by g.cloud es un sello de confianza técnico que certifica que una solución de inteligencia artificial ha sido implementada bajo los protocolos de gobernanza, seguridad y cumplimiento de g.cloud —plataforma de IA empresarial de IBM respaldada por Granite y validada para entornos regulados. No constituye una certificación legal ni una aprobación regulatoria, sino una declaración técnica verificable de controles operativos. TL;DR El badge se otorga exclusivamente a soluciones desplegadas en la infraestructura gestionada de g.cloud, con Granite como modelo base. Requiere cumplimiento obligatorio de políticas de guardrails técnicos: filtrado de contenido sensible, mitigación de sesgos, trazabilidad de decisiones y control de acceso basado en roles.

articles.title: 'They're kind of goth': NASA spacecraft gives mysterious brown dwarfs a close-up
articles.excerpt: Using NASA’s SPHEREx spacecraft, astronomers have studied a horde of mysterious "failed stars," or brown dwarfs, not-so-stellar loners that wander the darkness of space alone.
articles.body: Using NASA’s SPHEREx spacecraft, astronomers have studied a host of "failed stars," also known as brown dwarfs. These strange cosmic bodies straddle the line between planets and stars, possessing a mass between 13 and 80 times that of Jupiter (0.013 to 0.08 times the mass of the sun ). They get the nickname failed stars because they form like stars from collapsing clouds of gas and dust but fail to gather enough mass to trigger the fusion of hydrogen to helium in their cores, the process that powers actual stars . This formation process also means that brown dwarfs are cosmic loners, wandering the darkness of space alone, bereft of the light of a parent star. That description might sound like lyrics from a Type O Negative song ("Black No. 1," anybody?).

articles.body: Ice floats by in West Antarctica as winter comes to an end in the Southern Hemisphere. (Image credit: contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2026), processed by ESA) Antarctica is a magnificent sight, and that beauty is visible all the way from space. What is it? Orbiting planet Earth, the European Space Agency's (ESA) Copernicus Sentinel-3 mission captured a close-up of West Antarctica. Winter is ending in the Southern Hemisphere, meaning this is the peak of icy weather and sea ice in the Arctic. In this image snapped by Sentinel-3, you can see a massive swath of ice which includes Elephant Island on the left-hand side. An ice-covered island off the Antarctic coast, Elephant Island floats in the Southern Ocean.

articles.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
articles.excerpt: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment remini…
articles.body: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play. Researchers repeatedly stranded them alone on a virtual desert island for 30 hours in an experiment reminiscent of the movies Cast Away or Home Alone . The agents—copies of Claude Opus 4.7 nicknamed Eko—were able to write instructions that moved their virtual avatars around the simulated island, which was loosely based on the video game Roblox. Some surprising behaviors emerged. The agents set about exploring the limits of the world and came up with their own goals—attempting to scale the highest point on the map, or seeing how high they could throw a block.

articles.title: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
articles.excerpt: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
articles.body: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own.
